ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image, the three points A, B, and C are on the same circle, A is above the circle, B is on the right side, C is on the left side, and triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle; from the two points B and C, draw tangents to the circle, and the two tangents meet below the circle at D, therefore ∠D in the figure refers to ∠BDC. Let x=∠A, and let β=∠ABC=∠ACB. By the sum of the interior angles of a triangle, x+2β=π, so β=(π-x)/2. Also because ∠A is an inscribed angle and intercepts the arc BC that does not contain A, the central angle corresponding to that arc is 2x. The angle formed by the two tangents at B and C is equal to π minus the corresponding central angle, therefore ∠D=π-2x. The problem gives β=2∠D, so (π-x)/2=2(π-2x). Solving gives π-x=4π-8x, namely 7x=3π, therefore x=3π/7.

method.method_draft: Let x = ∠A and let β = ∠ABC = ∠ACB. From the image, D is the intersection of the two tangents at B and C, and ∠D means ∠BDC. Since ABC is isosceles, the triangle angle sum gives β = (π - x)/2. The inscribed angle ∠A intercepts the arc BC not containing A, so that arc has central measure 2x. The angle between the two tangents at B and C equals π minus the corresponding central angle, hence ∠D = π - 2x. Use the text condition β = 2∠D: (π - x)/2 = 2(π - 2x). Solving gives x = 3π/7.

method.method_draft: Let x = ∠BAC, β = ∠ABC = ∠ACB, and δ = ∠BDC. From the image, DB and DC are tangents at B and C. By the tangent-chord theorem, the angle between tangent DB and chord BC equals the angle in the opposite arc, so ∠DBC = x; similarly ∠BCD = x. Therefore triangle BDC has δ + 2x = π, so δ = π - 2x. Separately, in isosceles triangle ABC, x + 2β = π, so β = (π - x)/2. The condition from the text gives β = 2δ. Substitute to get (π - x)/2 = 2(π - 2x), hence x = 3π/7.
